source_caption:
On October 2, 1187, Salāh ad-Dīn led an army of 30,000 Muslims to retake Jerusalem from the Christians who had plundered it nearly a century earlier. His forces surrounded the city for nearly two weeks. Though vastly outnumbered, the 2,000 Christian defenders, led by Balian of Ibelin, fought fiercely before ultimately negotiating a surrender. 👀 ⁣⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣⁣
Unlike the Christians in 1099, who had massacred the city’s inhabitants, Salāh ad-Dīn chose mercy over bloodshed. He allowed the Christians to leave the city and return to their lands of origin, demonstrating a level of dignity and honor uncommon in that era. His conquest of Jerusalem would forever cement his legacy in human history. ⁣⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Salāh ad-Dīn‘s story is powerful depicted in Ridley Scott’s Director’s Cut of 𝐊𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐝𝐨𝐦 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐞𝐧 (𝟐𝟎𝟎𝟓). The director even disowned the theatrical version of the film because of inaccuracy and insists that his Director’s Cut is the only true and definitive version. ⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Rate 𝐊𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐝𝐨𝐦 𝐨𝐟 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐞𝐧 (𝟐𝟎𝟎𝟓) out of ten. 🔟

source_details.title: Kingdom of Heaven
source_details.synopsis: Kingdom of Heaven is a 2005 historical drama film directed and produced by Ridley Scott and written by William Monahan. It features an ensemble cast including Edward Norton, Orlando Bloom, Eva Green, Jeremy Irons, David Thewlis, Brendan Gleeson, Marton Csokas, and Liam Neeson. The film is a portrayal of the events leading to the Third Crusade, focusing mainly on Balian of Ibelin who fights to defend the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem from the Ayyubid Sultan Saladin. Filming took place in Ouarzazate, Morocco, and in Spain, at the Loarre Castle (Huesca), Segovia, Ávila, Palma del Río, and Seville's Casa de Pilatos and Alcázar.
